Jersey: A Pocket-Sized Motorcycle Paradise

Jersey is the largest of the Channel Islands — just 9 miles by 5 miles — sitting closer to France than England. Despite its tiny size, it offers a surprisingly rewarding motorcycle experience: dramatic clifftop roads, deep-cut valleys, WWII fortifications, and a relaxed pace of life that encourages exploration rather than speed.

Getting There

Condor Ferries operate from Poole to St Helier — about 4.5 hours on the conventional ferry or 3 hours by high-speed. The high-speed service accepts motorcycles. Book well in advance for summer — capacity is limited. Alternatively, Blue Islands and other airlines fly to Jersey Airport, and you can hire locally.

The North Coast

Jersey's north coast is the island's scenic highlight. The cliffs between Greve de Lecq and Rozel are spectacular, with headlands dropping hundreds of feet to the sea. The coast road winds through these headlands with frequent viewpoints. Stop at Devil's Hole — a dramatic blow hole carved by the sea. Bonne Nuit Bay and Bouley Bay are beautiful hidden harbours.

The Interior

Jersey's interior is a maze of Green Lanes — narrow lanes where pedestrians, cyclists, and horses have priority and the speed limit is 15mph. These lanes connect farms, manors, and medieval churches through a patchwork of small fields. On a motorcycle, they're charming and intimate — a world away from normal road riding.

Jersey feels like a piece of France that went British. The cuisine, the place names, and the climate are distinctly continental, but the pubs, post boxes, and politeness are unmistakably British.

WWII History

Jersey was occupied by Nazi Germany from 1940 to 1945 — the only British territory to be occupied. The War Tunnels (a massive underground hospital carved by slave labour) are a powerful and sobering experience. German bunkers and observation towers dot the coastline, many accessible from the road.

What to See and Do

  • Jersey War Tunnels — Underground hospital, the island's most important historical site
  • Mont Orgueil Castle — 13th-century fortress overlooking Gorey harbour
  • La Corbiere Lighthouse — Iconic lighthouse on the south-west tip, accessible on foot at low tide
  • Elizabeth Castle — Island fortress in St Aubin's Bay, reached by amphibious ferry
  • Royal Jersey Showground — Famous for Jersey cattle and cream

Practical Information

The speed limit on Jersey is 40mph maximum (15mph on Green Lanes). Fuel is cheaper than the UK mainland. The currency is the Jersey Pound (interchangeable with Sterling). Food is excellent — fresh seafood is a highlight. The island has a Mediterranean microclimate and is noticeably warmer and sunnier than the UK mainland. Allow 2-3 days to explore Jersey properly.

faq.q: How do I get to Jersey with my motorcycle?
faq.a: Condor Ferries operate from Poole to St Helier, taking about 4.5 hours on the conventional ferry or 3 hours by high-speed craft, which accepts motorcycles. Book well in advance for summer, as capacity is limited. Alternatively, fly into Jersey Airport with an airline such as Blue Islands and hire a bike locally.

faq.q: What is the scenic highlight of Jersey?
faq.a: The north coast is the island's scenic highlight. The cliffs between Greve de Lecq and Rozel are spectacular, with headlands dropping hundreds of feet to the sea and frequent viewpoints along the coast road. Stop at Devil's Hole, a dramatic sea-carved blow hole, and the hidden harbours of Bonne Nuit Bay and Bouley Bay.

Jersey's interior is a maze of Green Lanes, narrow lanes where pedestrians, cyclists and horses have priority and the speed limit is just 15mph. They connect farms, manors and medieval churches through a patchwork of small fields. On a motorcycle they are charming and intimate, a world away from normal road riding.

faq.q: What should I know about speed limits and fuel?
faq.a: The maximum speed limit on Jersey is 40mph, dropping to 15mph on the Green Lanes, so this is a destination for relaxed exploration rather than fast riding. Fuel is cheaper than on the UK mainland, and the currency is the Jersey Pound, which is interchangeable with Sterling.

faq.q: How long do I need, and what should I see?
faq.a: Allow 2 to 3 days to explore Jersey properly. The Jersey War Tunnels, an underground hospital carved by slave labour during the wartime occupation, are the most important historical site. Also visit Mont Orgueil Castle above Gorey, La Corbiere Lighthouse and Elizabeth Castle in St Aubin's Bay.
